articleTitle: Digital LED desk lamp with automatic uniform illumination area by using two accelerometers and halftone method
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we design a digital LED desk lamp that can adjust the LEDs brightness in the LED array to obtain the uniform illuminated area whenever the user rotates the lamp shade. The system contains three parts: the LED light source, the tilted measurement unit and the control unit. When the user adjusts the position of the lamp shade the system can change the halftone pattern by using the angle difference from the measurement of the two accelerometers to produce a uniform illuminated area.

articleTitle: Video tonal stabilization with automatic multiple anchor frames
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm to fix the tone inconsistency in captured video especially by mobile devices such as smartphone and black box cameras. We propose a method to stabilize the inconsistent tone of video frames in which tone is adjusted for each frame with adjustment map using several key anchor frames.

articleTitle: Concurrent Bluetooth module activation for reducing the latency of NFC connection handover
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In the current NFC connection handover protocol for Bluetooth, it takes impractically long time to make a Bluetooth connection between two devices since the Bluetooth modules of the devices are activated in a serial fashion. In order to resolve this problem, we propose a novel scheme for fast NFC-to-Bluetooth connection. We devise two new handover messages called Handover Query (HQ) and Handover Ack (HA) for the concurrent activation of Bluetooth modules and revise the current handover protocol to utilize HQ/HA messages. According to the evaluation results, the elapsed time to establish a Bluetooth connection is reduced by about 30%.

articleTitle: A hybrid selection method of helpful unlabeled data applicable for semi-supervised learning algorithms
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents an empirical study on selecting a small amount of useful unlabeled data with which the classification accuracy of semi-supervised learning algorithms can be improved. In particular, a hybrid method of unifying the simply recycled selection method and the incrementally reinforced selection method is considered and empirically evaluated. The experimental results, obtained using well-known benchmark data sets through semi-supervised support vector machines, demonstrate that the hybrid method works better than the traditional ones do in terms of classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved malicious code classification considering sequence by machine learning
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Classification of malicious code by machine learning gives more flexible and adaptable prediction result than by existing approaches [1]. But the approach just can identify looks-like malicious code instead of real malicious one. In this research, a novel method to reduce the vagueness in the classification by machine learning to consider code sequence.

articleTitle: Color fringe correction using guided image filtering
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Color fringe causes degradation of image quality when an image is obtained from a digital camera. This paper presents a computationally efficient color fringe correction method using a guided filter. Experimental results with a number of test images show the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of color fringe removal and the computational load.

articleTitle: Timing driven global router with a pin partition method for 3D stacked integrated circuits
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) integration technology packs together multiple active device dies, achieving a higher level of integration within a given footprint. However, due to an increase in the design volume and complexity, routing has become a challenging problem in 3D IC designs. In this paper, we propose a timing driven routing algorithm for 3D IC with a load balancing method that distributes the capacitance of the interconnections including TSV. In the load balancing step, the sink pins are partitioned to balance the loads within the routing tree. The routing trees are then created by merging the sub-trees that are generated with the balanced group.

articleTitle: Video completion using block matching for video stabilization
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a video completion algorithm using block matching for video stabilization. In order to fill in missing pixels, the proposed algorithm consists of three steps: i) mosaicking for covering the missing static, planar regions, ii) estimation of local motion vectors using the hierarchical Lucas-Kanade optical flow method, and iii) selection of the most similar patch in both spatial and temporal neighbors. The proposed video completion algorithm can be applied in the wide areas of consumer electronics including camcorders, smart phone cameras, tablet cameras, and smart glasses.

articleTitle: Implementation of cloud server for home screen based on smart TV
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we will propose cloud server for personalized home screen based on smart TV. We will describe the system architecture of the cloud server, home screen layout, data scheme of personalized home screen information, and show the result of editing home screen. We can delete an application, move their position, resized the window size of it, and delete the downloaded applications by editing functionalities.

articleTitle: AC-DC converter for wireless power transmission of energy harvesting system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this study, a high-efficiency AC-DC converter is developed for a wireless power transmission system that transmits power generated from energy harvesting. RF power is transmitted in the frequency of 10-100 MHz, and power of -10 to 15 dBm is received by the AC-DC converter. A matching network is designed according to the received power from resonant coils, and the load resistor is optimized to obtain maximum output power. As a result, conversion efficiency ranging from 50% to a maximum of 87% is achieved in an RF power range of -10 to 15 dBm that has 10-100 MHz frequency. Compared to other converters, the implemented AC-DC converter shows not only 20%-40% higher peak efficiency, but also 20%-50% higher average efficiency. It is suitable for application in wearable devices or body area networks.

articleTitle: Personalized health support system for elderly people based on an application for the web and smartphone
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We have developed an Elderly people Health Management System (EHMS) for the web and smartphones. The system acquires information about the individual, including information about basic physical strength, and provides services that can be used for personalized health management. In general, the management of physical exercises is targeted for physically handicapped or disabled population with limited clinical data in cases where the limited clinical data are not sufficient for prescribing a wide range of physical exercise elements. In our program, comprehensive physical information is provided to the specific user and data for 300 pre-archived physical exercises are used to construct instructions for physical exercises based on the user's personal requirements. The EHMS offers an algorithm to users, which is developed through our research, for individual physical exercises with scientific data analysis. Based on this algorithm, the subject's physical condition can be accurately analyzed and reflected in order to provide a suitable exercise prescription.

articleTitle: Parallel implementation of hybrid vector quantizer-based block truncation coding for mobile display stream compression
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a parallel implementation of hybrid vector quantizer-based block truncation coding using Open Computing Language (OpenCL). Processing dependency in the conventional algorithm is removed by partitioning the input image and modifying neighboring reference pixel configuration. Experimental results show that the parallel implementation drastically reduce processing time by 6~7 times with significant visual quality improvement.

articleTitle: An efficient spectrum sharing for throughput enhancement in heterogeneous networks
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Spectrum sharing has been considered as one of candidate technologies for enhancing spectral efficiency in wireless networks. Efficient cooperation among multiple radio access networks and proper system parameter setting regarding spectrum sharing are required in order to accomplish improvement on the system performance through spectrum sharing in such heterogeneous networks. This paper proposes a spectrum sharing scheme among access networks utilizing licensed and unlicensed band with an objective of enhancing system throughput while satisfying the user quality of service (QoS) under a simple condition of user deployment. A problem formulation to achieve the objective is suggested which enhances the system' spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Gradient local binary patterns for age group estimation
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new texture descriptor GLBP (Gradient LBP) for age group estimation. LBP exploits the only signs of the gradients between a center pixel and its surrounding pixels in a local patch and it does not reflect their magnitudes. This fails LBP to describe local signal structure in detail. Motivated by this observation, we propose so called GLBP, which considers the magnitude as well as the sign of the gradient. Experimental results show that when the proposed method is applied to age group estimation, it can achieve higher classification rate than existing well-known texture descriptors.

articleTitle: A FPGA based real-time post-processing architecture for active stereo vision
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a post-processing architecture for high quality depth map in active stereo vision. The proposed architecture consists of five sub-blocks in cascade manner, which are consistency check, hole filling, variance check, weighted median filter, and joint bilateral filter. The novel design which is implemented on a single FPGA achieves 60 frames per second for 1280×720 stereo images with 256 disparity range.

articleTitle: Digital signage system using virtualization technology
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we present a digital signage system that utilizes virtualization technology. In the proposed system, signage contents are played in a signage server. Screenshots of content are captured and transferred to a thin signage player. User interaction information is transferred from the signage player to the server. We have used the process based virtualization scheme for the system. The process based virtualization scheme requires less computational resources than the conventional virtual machine based virtualization scheme when serving multiple signage players.

articleTitle: Robust background generation using a modified mixture of Gaussian model for object detection
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a robust background generation method using a modified mixture of Gaussian model. Traditional background generation methods become unstable when the camera viewpoint suddenly changes. To solve this problem, the proposed method robustly extracts the background by mixing multiple Gaussian models.

articleTitle: An identification system using fingerprint for live broadcasting content On TV
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We propose a new identification system for live broadcasting content on TV in this paper. We exploit fingerprinting scheme for audio or video sequences to identify broadcasting content. Moreover, we decrease delay time after inserting fingerprint on DB in order to improve efficiency of a proposed system. The proposed system is composed of a registration server per one TV channel, an identification server with a director and workers, and many search clients. Simulation results show that the proposed system provides real-time processing performance on live broadcasting content on TV.

articleTitle: RF energy harvesting with W-CDMA
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The low power RF devices such as RFID and Zigbee are important for ubiquitous sensing. However, these devices are powered by a portable energy source like battery. Thus the usage of a low power RF device has limited. To mitigate this problem, we have developed RF energy harvesting with W-CDMA for a low power RF device. Diodes is required with low turn on voltage, since the diode threshold is larger than the received peak voltage of the rectenna. Therefore, we used a Schottky diode HSMS-286. The prototype of RF energy harvesting device shows the maximum gain of 5.8dBi for W-CDMA signal. The 16 patch antennas are manufactured with 10 dielectric constant PTFT board. In low power RF devices, transmitter requires the step-up voltage 2.5~5V with up to 35 mA. To meet this requirement, we used the Texas Instruments TPS61220 as a low input voltage step-up converter. From evaluated result, the achievable incident power of rectenna as 926mV to operate Zigbee can obtain within the distance of 12m.

articleTitle: Moving object detection using background subtraction and motion depth detection in depth image sequences
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We propose a novel method that detects moving objects in depth image sequences using background images and motion depth (MD) values. The background image represents the camera view with no moving objects and the MDs are the depth values of moving objects. Foreground regions can be easily detected by background subtraction; however, the foreground regions have some noise and do not contain a regional diffusion of depth values. Therefore, we apply both background subtraction and motion depth detection to detect moving objects. Experimental results show the proposed method robustly detects moving objects, even if the moving region exists in close proximity to the background surfaces. Therefore, the method can be widely used to detect moving objects in depth image sequences.

articleTitle: Post-processing algorithms for real-time active stereo vision
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents post-processing algorithms which work on a commercial FPGA for high quality stereo vision results. Specially, in this paper we focus the description of algorithms and their performance evaluation results instead of explaining hardware architecture. The proposed algorithms consists of five sub-blocks in cascade manner, which are consistency check, hole filling, variance check, weighted median filter, and joint bilateral filter. The experimental results show that error rates are 6.02% (6.57% with no using) for real world camera input(1280×720 intensity, maximum disparity 256), and 8.30% (13.7% with no using) for Middlebury stereo image set when we use the proposed post-processing.

articleTitle: Data-driven user feedback: An improved neurofeedback strategy considering individual variability of EEG features
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The aim of the present study was to develop a new neurofeedback strategy named the data-driven user feedback that considers individual variability of electroencephalography (EEG) features in order to make the users of the neurofeedback system experience wider range of feedbacks. Twenty healthy subjects performed a hidden catch paradigm, during which EEG signals were acquired from two prefrontal channels. From our experimental results, 72% increment in the number of valid (feedback) bins could be attained using the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Low-delay stream switch method for real-time transfer protocol
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: With wide spread of smartphones and high speed mobile communication technology, mobile broadcasting market is growing rapidly. Bit stream change during Video-on-Demand service causes large delay of video and audio playback, which makes user inconvenience. To avoid large delay, a method for low-delay stream switch is proposed and implemented on Android platform. Experimental result shows 72.71ms of stream change time on average when bit stream change occurred.

articleTitle: Fabricated RC-Pi type ESD/EMI filter based on transient voltage suppression diode for portable electronic applications
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: New RC-Pi type ESD/EMI filters were fabricated using the integrated passive devices technology. Unique TVS diodes were employed to improve the electrostatic discharge (ESD) strength of the filters without sacrificing capacitance. The fabricated filter device has a cut off frequency of 270 MHz and the attenuation higher than -30 dB at >1 GHz. ESD testing results demonstrated the filter was capable withstand ±10 kV of IEC 61000-4-2 and handle positive TLP current up to 19 A. This evidence that excellent ESD performance can be found in the filter consist of the small TVS diode dimension of 50×50 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The research results guide that employing TVS diodes are effective in the protection of data communication applications from very strong ESD shocks and noise disturbs.

articleTitle: Text detection in video sequence using 1-D DCT
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, a new method of detecting text regions from video sequences, without prior knowledge such as font, color, size of characters is proposed. By analyzing the characteristics of text regions in video sequences, we found that text regions include both horizontal and vertical edges simultaneously, while background regions do not. Therefore, In order to detect text regions accurately, the detection of candidate object regions through 1D-DCT and an adaptive thresholding technique are proposed. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method successfully detects text regions regardless of environmental conditions such as low contrast, complex texture, and various colors and sizes.

articleTitle: Per-block-group journaling for improving fsync response time
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The journaling is indispensable to the file systems of battery-backed consumer devices. It can cope with sudden power failures guaranteeing the file system consistency. However, the current compound transaction scheme can incur significantly long latencies for fsync system calls. This paper proposes a new more fine-grained journaling scheme called per-block-group journaling. Experiments show that the proposed scheme can reduce the average response time of fsync by up to 75%.

articleTitle: Device objectification for internet of things services
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Current internet is evolving into internet of things(IoT) which can connect various information(thing in itself and its sensing environment information). This paper suggests IoT service architecture which provides web base IoT services with various devices, web base IoT service platform which provides application services and object gateway which provides web connectivity to legacy devices.

articleTitle: Implementation of smart-learning education system using robotic pet
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: An edu-game (or edu-entertainment) is a method or program designed as educational software with entertainment factors which allows users to learn as they play a game. For such edu-game, the concentration ratio of targeted age group is a major consideration. This study describes how to realize an edu-game that can lead to body motions by using the software and robotic pet (hardware) at the same time in order to increase concentration of early childhood education. It also explains the interconnection structure of hardware - which uses Bluetooth of functions in a smart phone - and the edu-game and the algorithm to enhance the direction controller that has taken the working principle and user convenience into consideration.

articleTitle: A low-power second-order double-sampling delta-sigma modulator for audio applications
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-power double-sampling delta-sigma (ΔΣ) modulator for audio applications. The proposed modulator adopts a second-order cascade of integrators feedforward type and employs an adaptive current saving scheme for the low power operation. The adaptive current control logic senses the output transition of integrator and controls the bias current of operational transconductance amplifiers. The proposed ΔΣ modulator is fabricated using a 0.18-μm CMOS process. The measurement result shows that the power consumption of the proposed ΔΣ modulator is reduced from 2.57 mW to 1.93 mW without sacrificing the signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Local sparse representation optimized to edge orientation for inverse halftoning
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: A method is proposed for fully restoring local image structures of an unknown continuous-tone patch from an input halftoned patch with homogenously distributed dot patterns, based on locally learned dictionary pairs via feature clustering. Experimental results show that the use of the paired dictionary selected by the local edge orientation enables the restored continuous-tone images to include well-expressed fine details and outlines, especially in the areas of textures, lines, and regular patterns.

articleTitle: Speech playback geometry for smart homes
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Smart homes are environments that intelligently communicate with users, primarily through speech, to control various devices and activities relating to daily living. Both automatic speech recognition and text-to-speech are enabling technologies, however the basic home environment is often acoustically noisy and unconstrained in usage, leading to significant practical difficulties with both key technologies. In addition to interfering noise problems, a home occupant may not always be located physically close to either a microphone or loudspeaker. Speech intelligibility in a smart home depends on many factors including background noise, speech power and content. It is also affected by the orientation of the listeners' ears with respect to the speech source. This paper describes a simple technique to adjust perceived phase angle, and reports results from experiments to assess how the intelligibility of speech heard in such an environment will vary with respect to head position.

articleTitle: Mono-camera based vehicle detection using effective candidate generation
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel on-road vehicle detection algorithm for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems. The proposed algorithm uses shadow and edge information of original image to generate the candidate vehicles. The proposed algorithm extracts the shadow region darker than the road, and creates an edge image using the Canny edge detector. It performs AND operation between the shadow image and the edge image. The candidate vehicles are verified by SVM classifier based on the HOG feature vector. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm provides fast and accurate vehicle detection. And the number of candidates is reasonable for the vehicle verification.

articleTitle: Foreground extraction for real-time crowd analytics in surveillance system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive background modeling algorithm for crowd surveillance system. We employed Approximate Median Method (AMM) along with the Phase congruency edge detector to develop the background model. The resulting foreground of the proposed model was obtained by applying a logical AND operation between binary maps of the (foreground) of the AMM image and the gradient information of the (Phase congruency edge detector) PC. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is highly accurate while providing a processing speed of 24.8 fps allowing its implementation for real time application.

articleTitle: Content awareness-based color image enhancement
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a novel color image enhancement method to improve the image brightness based on retinex theory. Specifically, the proposed method employs an adaptive gamma correction on the illumination components based on pixels. We appropriately perform the brightness enhancement. Additionally, we restore the detail and color using reflectance components. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing algorithm in terms of subjective assessment and processing speed. Therefore, it can be applied effectively to outdoor vision applications or digital devices including mobile cameras and camcorders with low complexity.

articleTitle: A rectification method for quick response code image
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, a rectification method for quick response code (QR code) using kernel based Hough transform is proposed. The kernel based Hough transform shows significantly better performance than the standard Hough transform in terms of computational cost, while maintaining robust results. QR code consists of black and white modules. Morphological operations are applied to the QR code image as preprocessing to fill white modules with black modules. The boundary surrounding the QR code can be obtained using Kernel based Hough transform. Once the boundary is determined, the QR code image can be rectified by applying a perspective transformation to the image. Experimental results show that the proposed method can efficiently rectify QR Code images.

articleTitle: Ultra low capacitance bidirectional transient voltage suppression device for the protection high speed data line from electrostatic discharge shocks
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: New ultra low capacitance bidirectional transient voltage suppression (Bi-TVS) devices consist of two parallel unidirectional TVS devices facing opposite directions, have been fabricated for electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection applications. The reduced pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD) technology allows growing uniform thin Si films with various doping conditions and thicknesses of a PIN and TVS diode in one die. This result in a small turn on dynamic resistance of ∼0.7 Ω and leakage current below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> A. The employing PIN diode was effective in reducing the capacitance that suppressed down to ∼0.6 pF and in leading to the wide signal band pass over 3 GHz. The fabricated Bi-TVS device was capability handled the IEC 610004-2 peak voltage and TLP current in exceeding ±29 kV and ±30 A. The research results guarantee that the new proposed TVS device is very effective in protecting high speed data line against strong and rapid ESD attacks.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of FPGA-based transmitter memory management system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: FPGA is the first choice for developing the prototype system and the IP cores. Many existing network protocols are developed as IP cores, for example, the ethernet MAC open core. In this paper, an FPGA-based memory management system is proposed for the MAC protocol IP core, to facilitate the memory status acquisition and to support the functions in term of receiving packets from the upper layer, transmitting aggregated packets, and selectively re-transmitting the failed packets. The basic idea is to separate the packet management function from the packets store function of the memory system, where each buffer descriptor in the packet management block corresponds to a packet buffer in the packet store block. The design philosophy and the implementation details are presented.

articleTitle: Surface normal vector force driven 3D object reconstruction via Graph-cut
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Multi-view 3D surface reconstruction is typically formulated as minimizing an appropriate energy functional, which tends to find the empty set, i.e. an undesirable result, especially when cooperating only with a boundary term. So generally a regional term is employed, which indicates inside or outside of the surface. It is, however, the challenge because inherently there is no straightforward way to assign interior or exterior of the surface since photo-consistency on the surface boundary is the main source of geometric information. In this paper, we address this problem by proposing a surface normal vector force driven regional term which is a data-aware ballooning term and cast it into a Graph-cut framework. In experiments, we verify the superiority of the proposed algorithm on various multiple view data sets.

articleTitle: An improvement of audio transfer QoS over 802.11 WiFi Network environment
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: High quality wireless audio transfer is essential for external digital audio products. There are two kinds of methods for transferring audio data. One is using proprietary RF channel and protocol for reliable audio transfer, the other is using preexisting 802.11 WiFi Network. Audio transfer via WiFi network is more general and preferred method compared to proprietary wireless transfer. But when WiFi traffic is getting heavy, it is difficult to guarantee QoS of audio Data. In this paper, we have proposed independent data transfer using additional USB endpoint for ensuring QoS of data.

articleTitle: Resident-presence/absence estimation by unsupervised threshold learning for home energy consumption and its application to resident profiling
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We present a new method to estimate resident presence/absence status of a home using only home total power consumption data. The method is unsupervised in that the threshold computation for estimation is conducted without training data of presence/absence. From the estimation records collected for a certain period, we also automatically analyze a lifestyle profile of the residents living in the home.

articleTitle: Dependence of device performances on fin dimensions in AlGaN/GaN recessed-gate nanoscale FinFET
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this work, dependence of device performances on AlGaN/GaN heterostructure recessed-gate fin-shaped-channel field-effect transistor (FinFET), as a power transistor, on the fin dimensions is closely investigated. On-state (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>) and off-state (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub>) currents are affected by fin geometry and the former showed a more drastic change (250~1209 mA/mm) compared with the latter (confined to ~1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> mA/mm order). The design works have been conducted through a three-dimensional (3-D) technology computer-aided design (TCAD).

articleTitle: Undervoltage detector circuit for avionics using single supply voltage with MOS-FET
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Under-voltage detector (UVD) is consisted of the comparator and voltage divider, which is used for the reference and comparison with that reference in avionics. It is best for this UVD to use only one supply, but general UVD in commercial and avionics application has to use different supply for reference with comparator supply. This paper propose the advance UVD circuit, which use the threshold characteristics of MOS-FET, and makes it possible for UVD circuit to use only one supply for target and reference.

articleTitle: Handover scheme in a femto-cell system for peer-to-peer VoD download service
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we consider wireless P2P services based on femto-cell systems. In the wireless P2P system, changes in a network topology due to the handover have significant effects on the performance. We propose novel handover and cell management schemes in the femto-cell systems for peer-to-peer download service. The proposed schemes improve the download symbol rates and delay for handover in a P2P based VoD download service.

articleTitle: Quality-supporting duration in vehicle-to-vehicle cooperative communication with a decode-and-forward relaying vehicle
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a maximum allowable time that ensure a given outage probability target in vehicle-to vehicle cooperative communication (VVCC) with a decode-and-forward (DF) relay, which is referred to quality-supporting duration (QSD). QSD depends on the velocity of relaying vehicle and the initial positions of communicating vehicles. Numerical investigation shows how QSD greater than 200 seconds is achieved.

articleTitle: Non-destructive threshold assessment of a pinned photo diode pixel with correlated double sampling
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a pixel architecture and method of operation that enables a non-destructive assessment of the charge collected in a pinned photo diode pixel with transfer gate. The proposed architecture allows both true correlated double sampling for low noise at low light and per-pixel control of oversampling to increase the dynamic range of small pixels with limited full well capacity.

articleTitle: Process model verifier for integrated medical healthcare systems using business process management system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The integration of disparate medical healthcare systems such as hospital information system (HIS), radiology information system (RIS), and picture achieving and communication system (PACS) with the business process management system (BPMS) have garnered a considerable amount of attention for amalgamation with systems in external medical institutions. However, no effective process verification method exists in BPMS for medical healthcare systems, although considerable efforts have been expended on verification techniques in BPM research fields. In this paper, we propose a process model verifier that covers control-flow, data-flow, and business compliance rules for integrating medical healthcare systems using BPMS.

articleTitle: The reliability-enhanced wireless networks through BATS codes
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Network coding (NC) is a promising method used to achieve the channel capacity and enhance the reliability of multicast networks. However, the general wireless multicast networks based on NC are facing big problems such as long delays and large computational complexities. We propose a multicast network based on Batched sparse (BATS) codes which can efficiently solve these problems. Since fountain codes can also improve the reliability of wireless networks. We thoroughly compare the performance of BATS codes with that of fountain codes under our proposed networks. Simulation findings indicate that the proposed scheme results in much less transmission delay with minor complexity loss compared to fountain codes. Through analysis and simulation, we demonstrate that BATS codes perform much better than digital fountain codes in the aspects of throughput and overhead at the transmitter. It is also further shown that BATS codes are more robust against high packet loss.

articleTitle: Background music separation for multichannel audio based on Inter-channel Level Vector Sum
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, a Blind Source Separation (BSS) algorithm for multichannel audio contents is proposed. Unlike common BSS algorithms targeting stereo audio contents or microphone array signals, our technique is targeted at multichannel audio such as 5.1 and 7.1 ch audio. Since most multichannel audio object sources are panned using the Interchannel Level Difference (ILD), we employ the ILVS (Interchannel Level Vector Sum) concept to cluster common signals (such as background music) from each channel. Our proposed method can therefore separate a common audio signal from multiple channels with a lower computational complexity. Our multichannel audio content separation technique can be applied to an upmix system or a cinema audio system requiring multichannel audio source separation.

articleTitle: A serious game design for english education on Smart TV platform
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper we present a serious game design for HTML5 multi cross-platform environment. Previously existing application were restricted to their specific platforms and users could not enjoy them elsewhere (Smart phones, pc, Smart TV). In this paper we take advantage of the HTML5 multi cross-platform and make use of Smart TV technology in order to bring a new type of content to the big screen where more than one person can be involved, learn and enjoy.

articleTitle: A fast face detection method based on skin color and Adaboost
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This work aims at designing a face detection system with high speed of processing and a reduced number of false positives compared to the well known Haar feature-based face detector developed by Viola and Jones. In this method, HS channels of HSV color space are logically combined for skin-color region extraction, then a blob-contour-property based filtering is used to indicate the optimum ROI (regions of interest) on the original image and finally Adaboost is given the face candidates ROI for face presence confirmation if any. Our experiment has shown that the processing time is reduced around ten times compared to Adaboost used alone in which the whole image needs to be scanned.

articleTitle: An application to generate keyhole markup language file format from GPS location data
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Since information from GPS receivers is hardly understand by consumers, we propose an conversion application from raw location data to KML format file that can be applicable Google Maps. At first, we analyze geological data from GPS receivers and extract moving routes, time, and speed. Then we make a new KML file. Using placemark keyword, we represent all location data. Finally, we load the KML file onto Google Earth to evaluate conversion results.

articleTitle: A DTW gesture recognition system based on gesture orientation histogram
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Dynamic time warping algorithm is a pattern matching algorithm that allows a nonlinear stretching of the data. In a recognition system using a matching algorithm, data clustering methods are used to reduce the number of gesture templates in the database, and thus reduce the computational cost; however, the recognition rate is degraded. In this paper, we proposed a DTW gesture recognition system that uses orientation histogram for feature extraction and candidate selection based on weighted probability histogram comparison. Probability histogram is obtained from orientation histogram. Experiment has shown that our method reduces the process time while keeping robustness against accuracy loss due to clustering method.

articleTitle: FDR and HDR for AF relaying with QoS guarantees
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a full-duplex amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying with guaranteeing quality of service (QoS). In order to evaluate the QoS guaranteeing ability of FDR, we derive the effective capacity with considering residual self-interference. Based on the analysis and numerical results, it is verified that the stringent QoS constraint degrades effective capacity performance of full-duplex relay (FDR) more severely than that of half-duplex relay. The simulation results also show that the better link quality at S-R link is required in order to guarantee QoS constraint at FDR.

articleTitle: A hopping phase estimator for frequency hopped FM/BFSK signals
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We proposed a hopping phase estimator to demodulate the received signals without any information with respect to hopped frequency in frequency hopping spread spectrum systems. We deal with signals modulated as frequency modulation (FM) or binary frequency shift keying (BFSK) and hopped by frequency predetermined random sequence. The received signal is demodulated through two stages such as hopped frequency tracking and hopping frequency estimation in this paper. The former is accomplished by choosing the frequency component with maximum amplitude after taking discrete Fourier transform (DFT). The latter consist of difference product and down-sampling and estimates the phase generated by hopped frequency. We obtained the probability density function (pdf) and variance performance of the proposed phase estimator and confirmed that the analysis agreed with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Tag recommendation system for multimedia retrieval in mobile Environment
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Nowadays, due to the explosive growth of mobile devices, social networks and multimedia contents sharing systems have become increasingly popular. However, the characteristics of mobile devices and tags make it difficult to perform an accurate tag-based multimedia retrieval. In this paper, we propose a novel tag recommendation system for multimedia retrieval based on the user trust model which takes advantage of tag clusters of Flickr and visual similarity of multimedia. The proposed system makes it possible to provide the reliable and relevant tags to user in mobile environment.

articleTitle: Development of passive BCIs for user-state monitoring with smart IT systems
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This study demonstrates a feasible online user-state monitoring system using an affordable consumer-grade wireless brain wave headset. The system was able to track the workload level in real-time with approximately 78% accuracy.

articleTitle: Web-based transmission and playback system for multi-camera video
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: We present a novel web-based transmission and playback system for multi-camera video. The proposed system transmits a user-selected camera view video by DASH-based scheme. A transmitted video is streamed and played on the web-based video player. In the experimental test, user is able to get a selected camera viewpoint video about five times faster than conventional DASH scheme.

articleTitle: Study of GPU scalability
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: General-purpose Graphic Processing Units (GPGPUs) have been widely used to accelerate heavy compute-intensive applications. In a market the number of GPU cores on one chip are increased to maximize performance by exploiting thread-level parallelism (TLP). But memory system could be a bottleneck, and assigning more cores does not help faster execution. In this paper, we observe GPU core scalability issue, and analyze major causes of the performance degradation under many core configuration in perspective of memory latency.

articleTitle: Robust tracking with accurate scale estimation using errors of motion vectors
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for tracking with accurate scale estimation using motion vector errors. First we estimate an object displacement vector using the set of inlier motion vectors(VMF) filtered out by Median Flow tracker [2]. Then we calculate each motion vector error, i.e. the distance between each VMF and the estimated object displacement vector. 50 percent of VMF with large motion vector errors are excluded from VMF and the other vectors become candidate vectors. Next, the scale change ratios of the object are calculated using candidate vectors. We calculate the errors of scale change ratio using the median of scale change ratios, using the same method as we did for motion vector errors. Finally, if the median of ratio errors is lower than a threshold value, the median of scale change ratios is decided to the object scale change ratio. Otherwise the object scale is maintained to the next frame.

articleTitle: User interface evaluation method using eye tracking
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, We measured the relationship between game UI and graphics playing mobile game using in eye tracking technology and verified that user interface arrangement useful to design game is important factor according to the experimental results.

articleTitle: Forward projection model for noisy computerized tomography projection enhancement
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The noise in a low-radiation dose can be enhanced by an iterative reconstruction technique using forward and back projection models. This work investigated an iterative reconstruction approach using a forward projection model based on a contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE). Using the CLAHE technique, the projection image was processed to remove the noise, and then the preprocessed image was used as input to reconstruct the slice images. Finally, we evaluated the proposed method and found that compared to conventional reconstruction techniques, the proposed method led to improved image quality, concurrent with a reduction in the Poisson noise distribution, as demonstrated by phantom studies.

articleTitle: Development of millimeter-wave communication modem for mobile wireless backhaul
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Cellular communications are optimized for the low mobility users and their performances are degraded at high speed. So passengers in a high-speed train (350 km/h) experience very poor radio link qualities. This paper proposes mobile wireless backhaul based on millimeter-wave for mobile hotspot network. Prototype of the baseband modem was presented and the downlink/uplink performances for high-speed trains were analyzed in Rician fading channel conditions.

articleTitle: Frequency hopping mobile ad hoc network and adjacent channel interference implementation in NS-2
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The event-driven network simulator NS-2 does not support frequency hopping (FH) and multi-channel operations, as well as the adjacent channel interference (ACI), in its current form. This paper introduces the key implementation methods to enable FH mobile ad hoc network (MANET) simulations in NS-2. The proposed simulator provides proper analysis in arbitrary topologies of FH-MANET.

articleTitle: Annotation creation and representation system of sensory effects based on MPEG-V
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In a case of adding sensory effect metadata to media and generating sensory experience based media to provide a sensory experience media service, this paper provides a method of generating an annotation of to a sensory effect to enable a user to add the sensory experience metadata faster and more easily and conveniently, and a method of generating the sensory effect metadata based on the generated annotation.

articleTitle: Extended version of sphere decoding with MMSE based enumeration for DL MU-MIMO systems
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an extended version of sphere decoder (ESD) with the MMSE based enumeration for DL MU-MIMO systems. In previous work, we proposed the ESD which detects interference signals additionally. The ESD can achieve near-optimal performance, but it has much higher complexity than the existing SD. Therefore, this paper presents the improved enumeration based on MMSE. The proposed algorithm can reduce the complexity of ESD significantly while having low performance degradation.

articleTitle: Memory-efficient background subtraction for battery-operated surveillance system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Background subtraction is widely used in battery-operated surveillance system. In the system, memory requirement and computational complexity are important issues due to a constraint of the hardware resource. We propose memory-efficient and low computational complexity background subtraction algorithm based on multi-background registration (MBR) technique algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel peer-to-peer protocol for a selective VoD service in live streaming sessions
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to provide a selective VoD service in live streaming environment using peer-to-peer communications. The proposed scheme defines a peer classification method and a video frame sharing method to decrease peer side traffic burden. The proposed scheme can decrease the peer generating traffic overhead compared to the conventional peer-to-peer live streaming protocol.

articleTitle: Adaptive power management in LTE terminal modem
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: The high-speed communication environment and high-performance mobile devices have leveraged each other. Long Term Evolution (LTE) supports high bandwidth and low latency for data transfer. However, high bandwidth transfer will spend the mobile device's battery power rapidly. To extend the user equipment (UE)'s battery life time, LTE adopts enhanced Discontinuous Reception (DRX) mechanism. Even though LTE supports DRX framework to reduce power consumption, DRX not only depends on base-station but also needs sufficient idle time to operate efficiently. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive power management technique of LTE model which reduces the active (i.e. non-DRX period) power consumption. Our experimental results shows that a communication modem with the proposed method improves energy saving by 40.72% compared to previous modem.

articleTitle: Optimum relay sharing with statistical channel information in multiple-sensor relaying networks
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a multiple-sensor relaying network where a relay helps multiple sensor-destination pairs. We propose probabilistic relaying scheme and provide an optimal relay sharing ratio for the proposed scheme. Based on statistical channel information, the maximum outage probability between all users is minimized. Numerical results show that the proposed probabilistic relaying scheme outperforms no-relay scheme and exclusive relaying scheme .

articleTitle: Implementation of the web media transfer system for multi-screen services
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a web-based system that performs web media transfer across multiple screen devices using the collaboration service technologies.

articleTitle: Viewing angle calculation of display devices
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper introduces a method of calculation of a wide viewing angle for a 3D TV video wall using the height and the number of display devices used for displaying the 3D contents. The proposed viewing angle calculation is basically designed to reduce the crosstalk issue when the viewer's eye level is not in the middle of the 3D video wall screen standing in the fixed position. The principal of the proposed system is explained about the calculation of viewing angle for a 3D TV video wall.

articleTitle: ADC-free digital-control switch-mode LED driver with high switching frequency
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: A new ADC-free digital-control switch-mode LED driver with 1MHz switching frequency is presented, which is featured by digital counters, a PWM generator, and current comparators. The digital counter consists of up/down counters with a delay routine. The counter increases or decreases its binary value, depending on comparison result between the output current and the desired current. Then a PWM signal can be generated, which its pulse width is determined by multiplication of the binary value and the clock period. To prevent oscillation of the counter value owing to high frequency clock, a delay routine is added. This designed LED driver is successfully implemented through a 0.35μm 2poly-4metal high voltage process.

articleTitle: Adjustment of brightness contrast for fatigue decrease in stereo image production
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: A typical method of improving the contrast of images is HE(Histogram Equalization). This method makes uniform distribution by adjusting the histogram. However, this method is not concerned about the human visual system so as to cause visual fatigue in stereo image. In this paper, we propose a method for distinguishing object from background in image based on Roberts edge detection. The experiment result validates that our proposed algorithm is reliable to achieve brightness contrast ratio of 30% between main object and background image. Based on this adjustment on brightness contrast ratio, our stereo image can obtain a more comfortable stereo image with a less visual fatigue.

articleTitle: The analytic system of level design in FPS games: Focused on cover patterns
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: While the game design is the documentation of rules of a game play, the level design is the visualization of how a player confronts such rules. That is, it is about designing an environment (game levels) in which the player and the game interact in order to achieve the goal of the game. This study suggests an analytic system of level design for FPS games. Based on this system, it collects data on the player's behavior toward the cover pattern, which is one of the elements of level design, to immediately verify the game play intended by the game designer and describes a method to quantitatively compare.

articleTitle: Drain current improvement using spacer and charge plasma concept
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed the new structure of T-FET and analyzed the impact of spacer dielectric, device width, metal electrodes and temperature on Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (T-FET). A numerical TCAD device simulator 3-D ATLAS version 2.10.18.R shows that reducing the width will reduce the effective threshold voltage. Transistor with a high I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub> /I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub> ratio of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> sub-threshold swing of 54 mV/dec for the channel length of 50 nm with Hafnium oxide as gate dielectric material of thickness 3 nm and spacer dielectric as the silicon dioxide material.

articleTitle: Prefilter algorithm based on locally adaptive integer bilateral filter
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, a locally adaptive prefilter based on bilateral filter for the HD call is proposed. If the input sequences contain noises such as CCD noise, the performance of video compression is degraded. In order to solve this problem, we designed the prefilter that denoises the noise of the original input image before performing the video codec. The experimental results show that more than 14% bitrate saving on the average in the same MOS condition.

articleTitle: Resolution enhancement using direction information for cloud networks by selective interpolation
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel resolution enhancement method for cloud networks by selective interpolation. Resolution up-sampling algorithms for high quality should require high complex processing. To realize real time services, we propose the up-sampling method processed in cloud and client by off-loading. In the experimental results, the efficiency of the proposed method is shown by the comparison of processing times and peak signal to noise ratio.

articleTitle: Cooperative spectrum sensing using frequency domain correlation detection
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a cooperative spectrum sensing scheme for cognitive radio based on the FFT energy detection. The proposed cooperative sensing scheme utilizes the cross correlation between the output of the sensor of interest and composite output of other sensors. Simulation results show that the proposed cooperative sensing scheme is superior to conventional cooperative sensing using frequency domain correlation detection.

articleTitle: A comparison of multi-resolution stereo matching methods
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper implements four interpolation methods to modify the adaptive support weight (ASW) algorithm in multiresolution image representation. The disparity values at lower resolution level are used to determine disparity values of undetermined pixels at higher level during the interpolation procedure. The first interpolation method fills an undetermined pixel (a gap) with the averaged disparities of neighboring pixels. The second method examines the degree of color similarity between neighboring pixels. The similarity is used in neighboring disparity interpolation. The third method computes the disparity of the gap with ASW. The last method computes the disparity of the gap by considering minimum and maximum disparity values of neighboring pixels.

articleTitle: Compact video signatures for near-duplicate detection on mobile devices
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on generating compact but efficient video signatures on mobile devices so that users quickly know whether there are near-duplicates in the social network systems when they upload a video. For this, the proposed method employs the idea of inverted index that is one of the most popular text retrieval methods. Experimental results show that our method can achieve similar results compared with state-of-the-art method whereas it requires low memory and computation cost.

articleTitle: The design of DC-DC Converter with DT-CMOS Switch
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper is proposed DC-DC Converter with DT-CMOS (Dynamic Threshold voltage MOSFET) Switch. The proposed circuit is evaluated and compared with CMOS switch by both circuit simulation and device simulation. DT-CMOS switch reduces the output ripple and the conduction loss through a low on-resistance. Therefore, proposed converter has a excellent performance efficiency than converter with conventional CMOS switch. Proposed converter has switching frequency of 1.2MHz, 3.3V input voltage, 2.5V output voltage, and maximum current of 100mA. Also, this paper proposes two protection circuit in order to ensure the reliability. The first function is UVLO(under voltage lockout) and the second function is TSD(thermal shutdown). So, proposed converter can be protected from input under-voltage and over temperature.

articleTitle: Issues and challenges of real-time flash storage
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Existing studies on flash storage have mainly focused on high performance and reliability. A new quality metric, real-time performance, has recently been required from both data centers and mobile devices. For data centers, it should be able to provide an illusion that each virtualized runtime environment has a dedicated storage on top of a single shared storage. In mobile devices, multimedia applications such as camcorders require uniform response times from the storage to avoid frame skipping. This paper addresses issues and challenges in designing real-time flash storage. Our investigation leads us to conclude that it is important to make the storage analyzable in terms of request response times while exploiting the chip-level parallelism as much as possible.

articleTitle: Video contrast adjustment using spatio-temporal histogram specification
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Histogram specification based image contrast enhancement algorithms have been studied extensively. A recently presented 2-D histogram specification (2-D HS) scheme defines 2-D histogram from an input image and derives pixel-value mapping relationship using the 2-D histogram. In this paper, we apply the conventional 2-D HS to the temporal domain to adjust the spatio-temporal contrast of video signals. Our 2-D histogram is thus defined in the spatio-temporal domain, and the pixel values are adjusted using the spatio-temporal 2-D HS. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Exhibition method of hierarchical structure of Web communities using community density for Web video retrieval
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we present an exhibition method of hierarchical structure of Web communities using community density for Web video retrieval. In the proposed method, Web communities that are Web video sets with similar topics is hierarchically extracted by using hyperlinks between Web videos and their video features, and density of each Web community is estimated. Then we exhibit the hierarchical structure of Web communities according to the obtained density to users. Since users can grasp detail degree of topics contained in each Web community, the desired Web community can be easily selected for Web video retrieval.

articleTitle: O2-Enhanced surface treatment of Ge epitaxially grown on Si for heterogeneous Ge technology
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this work, in order to investigate the effects of annealing gases on the quality of Ge epitaxially grown on Si substrate, ex-situ rapid thermal annealing (RTA) processes with different gases have been performed. The Ge-on-Si samples were prepared by different growth techniques using reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD), and then, samples annealed in the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, forming gas (FG), and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> were compared with an unannealed one to confirm the improvements in Ge quality. To evaluate the material quality, photoluminescence (PL) measurements have been carried out for the samples at room temperature. Among the prepared samples, the O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-annealed sample showed the highest PL signals regardless of growth techniques, which supports that an ex-situ RTA in the O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ambient would be an effective technique for surface treatment of Ge in the fabrication processes of Ge-based electronic and photonic devices.

articleTitle: Converged media streaming and playback services across multiple media devices in home networks
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a new UPnP-compatible mechanism for enabling converged media streaming and playback services across multiple media devices in home networks. This mechanism design comprises three functional entities, including the UPnP AV media server, UPnP AV device controller, and converged media proxy. The functionality of this mechanism can accommodate heterogeneity of media content formats, transport protocols, and presentation styles among different media devices, thereby offering better user experience for home AV entertainment in residential environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wi-Fi data interruption and handover decision parameters
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, IEEE 802.11 based Wi-Fi data interruption situations are categorized for effective handover decision into moving out of coverage, initial attachment, congestion, and sudden disconnection. In addition, this paper analyzes representative handover decision parameters based on effect on data interruption time.

articleTitle: Recognition of severely distorted license plate numbers: Part 2 applications
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of recognizing severely distorted license plate numbers in the sense of resolution, illumination, and geometric transformations. The proposed recognition method first estimates degradation parameters from an input image. Next, a set of reference images are transformed using the estimated degradation parameters. The recognized number is then obtained by comparing the input image with the transformed version of reference numbers. Experimental results demonstrate this work enables to recognize numbers acquired in a critical condition.

articleTitle: Implementation of an MU-MIMO system with GPU modem for non-codebook-based TDD LTE-A
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: Recently, 3GPP disclosed MU-MIMO as an enhancement of Release10 for the target data rate of LTE-A. In this paper, we present a prototype implementation of 4×4 MU-MIMO system using a GPU-based modem for TDD LTE-A. As GPU handles a number of data simultaneously with the parallel processors, we have verified that the implemented MU-MIMO test-bed system can provide a real-time processing of LTE-A data with nearly 4 times larger throughput compared to Release10 SU-SISO system or 2 times compared to Release8 2×2 MU-MIMO system.

articleTitle: Algorithm of aiming point calibration in arcade gun using infrared LED and Wiimote camera module
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: An arcade gun has been one of game controllers activated in video game markets since 1970s. The arcade gun partially used in home video game console and penny arcade is utilized as interface for realistic media and interactive system in recent days. However, the conventional arcade gun has a disadvantage that it cannot be used in large screen due to restriction of hardware and cannot be applied to various contents as an independent module due to platform dependency. This paper establishes an arcade gun system based on infrared camera to solve this disadvantage, and proposes a interpolation algorithm that can be applied to various environments.

articleTitle: Blind bandwidth extension for codebook-based Bayesian speech enhancement
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a blind bandwidth extension (BBE) technique that improves the quality of narrowband (NB) speech signal enhanced by the codebook-based Bayesian speech enhancement method with minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimate. The MMSE weight vector of the NB speech envelope codebook is used to estimate the wideband (WB) speech envelope. An adaptive double shifting method is introduced in the BBE to obtain an enhanced WB excitation signal. Its performance is assessed via the log-spectral distortion (SD) and informal listening tests.

articleTitle: Analyses on ZnO/CdS heterojunction for design of CIGS photovoltaic device with higher accuracy
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this work, ZnO films were prepared by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and CdS films were deposited using chemical bath deposition (CBD) to form a ZnO/CdS heterojunction in the Cu(In,Ga)Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (CIGS) solar cell. More accurate mapping of band arrangement in the ZnO/CdS heterojunction has been performed by studying both its electrical and optical characteristics in depth by various analysis methods including transmittance, sheet resistivity measurement, and photoemission spectroscopies. Energy-band structures of the ZnO/CdS heterojunction could be accurately drawn from the extracted parameters taking the conduction band offset (CBO) into account. Consequently, a delicate description of the energy-band structure of the heterojunction has been made possible in this study, which would help acquisition of the full band structures of the thin films in the CIGS solar cell device and contribute to its reliable design with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Outage probability of a two-way relaying with cochannel interference
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper investigates the two-way relaying (TWR) with cochannel interference (CI). We study the effect of the CI on the outage probability of the TWR. It is shown that the outage probability increases as the number of interferers increases. The analytical results are verified with computer simulations.

articleTitle: Efficient test bitstream generation method for verification of HEVC decoders
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, a method to generate test bitstreams for verification of HEVC decoders is described, in which syntax elements (SEs) are classified into two classes: high-level and low-level. To enhance the coverage of high-level SEs, their values are selected by varying the structure of the bitstream and the combination of coding tools although the values of low-level SEs are decided by a method based on the constrained-random generation. The test bitstreams for the HEVC decoders generated by the proposed method have the SE coverage of 92.6%.

articleTitle: Multiple-emotion recognition using an avatar in mobile environments
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes a multiple emotion recognition system that can recognize combined emotions up to a maximum of three emotions using an active appearance model, the proposed classification standard, and k-Nearest Neighbor in mobile environments. To be easily understood, the recognized result is presented in three ways on a mobile camera screen. We can achieve the best 93% accuracy in recognizing the emotion of surprise.

articleTitle: Object retrieval using scene normalized human model for video surveillance system
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper presents a human model-based feature extraction method for a video surveillance retrieval system. The proposed method extracts, from a normalized scene, object features such as height, speed, and representative color using a simple human model based on multiple-ellipse. Experimental results show that the proposed system can effectively track moving routes of people such as a missing child, an absconder, and a suspect after events.

articleTitle: Histogram based dynamic range compression method using simple locality consideration
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we present a local dynamic range compression method based on a computationally efficient histogram. The proposed method classifies input image into three regions using simple statistical analysis and generates scene adaptive tone mapping curves for each region. Moreover, dynamic range compression output is calculated based on the characteristic of local region and scene adaptive tone curves. Finally, we compare our method with other histogram based tone mapping approaches.

articleTitle: Reusable DCT architecture for parallel processing of Y, U and V transforms in HEVC
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In 2D Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) hardware, most of the transpose memory remains unutilized when the size of input is smaller than the maximum supported size. This paper proposes a scheme for the DCT module in the HEVC encoder to exploit this unused memory and thus, to increase throughput through parallel processing. In the proposed architecture, transforms of Y, U and V residual blocks for TUs (Transform Units) smaller than 32×32 can be calculated in parallel. Experimental results show that a significant number of cycles are saved when compared to a conventional serial DCT hardware at a marginal increase in hardware cost.

articleTitle: Frame detection for DVB-S2 based time slice
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: In this paper, we firstly attempt to design initial acquisition schemes for wideband DVB-S2 based time slice transmission that was published recently. This provides the essential guideline to learn frame detection design for time slice DVB-S2 reception.

articleTitle: Optimized USB 2.0 scheduler for low latency data transfer
publicationTitle: The 18th IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Electronics (ISCE 2014)
abstract: This paper proposes two unique optimization techniques over USB 2.0 scheduler for addressing low latency requirement of embedded systems. The first optimization technique proposes the new priority based scheduling algorithm of USB 2.0 scheduler for non-periodic data transfer. The second technique is a simple insertion algorithm for scheduling periodic data transfer in USB 2.0 scheduler. The capability of this work is demonstrated over a Linux system prototype, for which we have encouraging results.
